subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should this PR continue as a narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool feature, or should cross-gateway messaging wait for the broader federation contract tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically repairable in places, but accepting the feature chooses a new cross-Gateway sender identity, credential, session ownership, and message-delivery boundary that automation cannot set safely.

options.title: Pause for federation/security design
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43605 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 to settle the trust model before merging this narrow PR.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow peer path
options.body: Allow this PR to continue only after the idempotency, explicit-auth, tests, docs, conflicts, and live multi-gateway proof are fixed.

options.title: Close this implementation path
options.body: If maintainers do not want `gateway.peers` as a core surface, close this PR and keep the issue/design trackers for a different implementation.

recommendation.title: Pause for federation/security design
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43605 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 to settle the trust model before merging this narrow PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history shows direct work on both Gateway auth recovery and the sessions_spawn/session-management surfaces involved in this boundary decision.
